segments.heading: Header and includes
segments.text:
- The file holds three candidate forms of the copy kernel `k_copy` of bandwidth.c.
- The file is only compiled: run_kernels.sh compiled it to an object file and printed the machine code [Ref1]. The file has no `main`, and no program calls its functions.
- `arm_neon.h` gives the vector type `uint64x2_t` and the NEON intrinsics `vld1q_u64` and `vst1q_u64`.

segments.heading: Macro `LOADS`: 16 vector loads (256 B)
segments.text:
- Declares 16 variables `v0` to `v15`. Each is one `uint64x2_t`: two 64-bit integers, 16 B.
- `vld1q_u64(P + k)` loads 16 B from the address of word `k` after `P`.
- The offsets 0, 2, ..., 30 cover 32 words (256 B) with no gap.

segments.heading: Macro `BARRIER`: an empty asm statement with 16 inputs
segments.text:
- An inline-assembly statement with an empty instruction text (`""`). It adds no instruction to the machine code.
- It names `v0` to `v15` as inputs. The constraint `"w"` asks for each value in a vector register.
- So the compiler must have all 16 loaded values in registers at this point [Ref3].
- The statement does not fix the order of the loads and the stores. The comment in bandwidth.c says that gcc may move code across it [Ref3].
- `volatile` tells the compiler that it must not delete the statement.
- The new read kernel `k_read` of bandwidth.c has the same statement. There it keeps the compiler from deleting the 16 loads [Ref3].

segments.heading: Macro `STORES`: 16 vector stores (256 B)
segments.text: `vst1q_u64(P + k, v)` stores the 16 B of `v` at word `k` after `P`. The 16 stores write `v0` to `v15` to the same offsets that `LOADS` read from.

segments.heading: Candidate 1 `copy_barrier`: loads, barrier, stores
segments.text:
- `d` is the destination, `s` the source, `n` the count of 64-bit words. `restrict` is the promise that the two buffers do not overlap.
- The source text of one loop pass has the 16 loads from `sp` (256 B), then `BARRIER`, then the 16 stores to `dp` (256 B). Then both pointers move by 32 words.
- The loop is `do ... while`: the body runs before the first test. `n` must be a multiple of 32 and not zero.
- These are the statements of `k_copy` in bandwidth.c [Ref3].
- Machine code of 2026-11-13: per loop pass all 8 `ldp` come before the 8 `stp`. It is the same instruction sequence as `k_copy` in bw_new [Ref2].

segments.heading: Candidate 2 `copy_plain`: no barrier
segments.text:
- The same loop without `BARRIER`.
- Machine code of 2026-11-13: loads and stores alternate. One loop pass has 8 `ldp`, 7 `stp` and 2 `stur` [Ref2].

segments.heading: Candidate 3 `copy_plain_norestrict`: no barrier, no `restrict`
segments.text:
- The same loop as candidate 2, but the pointers are not `restrict`.
- The compiler must then assume that a store to `d` can change bytes that a later load from `s` reads. So it cannot move a store to a place before a load.
- Machine code of 2026-11-13: per loop pass all 8 `ldp` come before the 8 `stp`, the same order as candidate 1 [Ref2].
